plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: Huge blush-pink and white blooms rise on tall stalks above round, waxy leaves that bead water like quicksilver. The flowers open at dawn and perfume the still summer air over ponds and wetlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August, so early August is in the flowering window
plants.location: Temperate East Asia, including the ponds and moats of Japan and China
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a microscopic texture that sheds water and dirt. This 'lotus effect' has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.

plants.name: Banksia spinulosa
plants.description: Slender golden-orange flower spikes up to 18 cm long bristle with dark maroon, hook-shaped styles. They glow in the winter bush and draw honeyeaters, bees and other nectar-feeders when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn and winter, which covers early August in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Eastern Australia, New South Wales and Queensland
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are often held closed by the plant until fire passes. The heat releases the seeds onto freshly cleared, nutrient-rich ground.

plants.name: Lavandula × intermedia
plants.description: Tall, silvery-green mounds send up long spikes of violet-blue flowers that hum with bees. In summer the scent drifts across fields and gardens, and the plants are farmed in rows for their essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to August, so early August falls within the flowering window
plants.location: Southern Europe, especially the lavender fields of Provence in France, and gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Lavandin is a natural hybrid of English lavender and spike lavender. It is sterile but vigorous, and it produces much more oil than either parent.
